We can introduce you to a suitable UK fertility clinic, which will quote you directly, with prices on application.

context_heading: Understanding licensing when you look for a clinic near you
context: Clinics that freeze eggs must be licensed by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority (HFEA). The HFEA's Choose a Fertility Clinic tool lets you look up each licensed clinic and see its inspection ratings, success rates and patient feedback, which is a useful way to check a clinic you are considering near you.

Some simple tests, such as blood hormone checks, may be offered outside HFEA licensing, but anything involving eggs, sperm or embryos should always be with a licensed centre. It is worth confirming the licence before you book anything, especially if a clinic is convenient but unfamiliar to you.

questions: Is this clinic licensed by the HFEA for egg freezing and storage?

faqs.q: Do egg freezing clinics need a licence?
faqs.a: Yes. Clinics that freeze eggs must be licensed by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority (HFEA). You can check any clinic you are considering using the HFEA's Choose a Fertility Clinic tool.

faqs.q: How do I judge a clinic near me?
faqs.a: Look at the HFEA's inspection ratings, success rates and patient feedback for each licensed clinic you are considering. It also helps to ask about storage fees and thaw survival rates directly, so you can compare on the things that matter to you.

faqs.q: What should I ask about storage?
faqs.a: Ask what the storage fees are, how they are charged and what the consent forms say about storage. It is worth understanding what happens if you later want to use your eggs or move them elsewhere.

faqs.q: Will iComply advise me on egg freezing?
faqs.a: No. We are an introduction service and do not give professional advice or provide treatment. We introduce you to a suitable UK fertility clinic, which will discuss your situation and quote you directly, with prices on application.
